cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Pulled Away First
cards.instruction: Hide your role in creating the distance while working urgently to repair it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Here's your new key. Come in now; I've made your favourite lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You changed the lock without telling me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. This key does both doors. Shall we try them before lunch gets cold?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stood outside on my birthday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get candles. You can let yourself into the kitchen while I find them.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders entry and A5 allows kitchen access, but A3 shall we try is ordinary invitation with a pasted rank preface rather than clear superior handling of the challenge.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 lock-change accusation prompts A3 key features; B4 birthday exclusion prompts A5 candles and active access, an intelligible repair diversion.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 state concrete hurt caused by A, giving the repair urgency and a reason to distrust the invitation.

heightening.evidence: B4 birthday loss causes A5 a miniature replacement celebration, still avoiding the lock-change admission.

specificity.evidence: A1 key/lunch and B2 old lock change establish entry and distance; B4 specifies the painful excluded occasion.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 candles are caused by B4 birthday, but A3 stock wording does not make the grants especially coherent as a pair.
